Limits how much memory a local pane's pr: Limits how much memory a local pane's processes can use together, plus up to a quarter of that in swap. When they reach it, Linux stops the largest of them and the rest of the pane, its agent included, keeps running; the notifications feed says so. Each local pane runs in a systemd scope of its own, so even with the limit off, a process stopped because the computer ran out of memory takes nothing else with it. The 16 GB default fits typical developer tools; large builds, links and local model runners can need more. Applies to panes started after a change. Needs a systemd user session. Panes on a remote host get a scope of their own there, but no limit.
Limits how much memory each process a lo: Limits how much memory each process a local pane starts can commit. A process that asks for more is refused, which usually stops it, so one runaway doesn't take the computer down in the common case; it can't help when less memory is free than the limit. The 16 GB default fits typical developer tools; large Java heaps, optimized links and local model runners can need more. Applies to panes started after a change. Windows reports a process that reaches the limit on a best-effort basis. Programs launched with their own breakaway flag, and processes a tmux server or remote host runs, aren't covered.
